When the budget module is present the\nfactory wraps the backend transparently.\n\nArgs:\n    backend: Concrete backend the factory built.\n    config: Mapping derived from ``payload.json``.\n    backend_identifier: Normalized backend identifier.\nReturns:\n    Either the wrapped proxy or the raw backend when the budget\n    module is not importable.", "kind": "method", "line": 354, "name": "_wrap_with_budget", "signature": "def _wrap_with_budget(backend, config, backend_identifier)"}, {"doc": "Return a concrete :class:`AIModel` selected by configuration.\n\nThe selection order is:\n\n1. Explicit ``backend`` argument when provided.\n2. ``llm_backend`` key from ``config`` (or loaded ``payload.json``).\n3. :data:`DEFAULT_BACKEND` (``\"auto\"``).\n\nWhen the resolved backend is ``\"auto\"`` the factory tries Groq first\n(if an API key is available) and falls back to Ollama. Any other\nexplicit selection is honoured strictly: callers receive\n:class:`LLMBackendUnavailableError` rather than a silent fallback so\nthey can decide whether to degrade or raise.\n\nThe returned backend is wrapped with the budget proxy so the daily\ncost cap and the per call token cap are enforced at the single\nchokepoint the framework uses. Use :func:`get_llm_backend_raw` to\nbypass the wrapper for tests that need a raw backend.\n\nArgs:\n    config: Optional pre-loaded payload mapping. When ``None`` the\n        payload is read from disk.\n    backend: Optional override for the backend identifier. Takes\n        precedence over the configuration value.\n\nReturns:\n    A configured :class:`AIModel` instance that also structurally\n    satisfies :class:`core.protocols.LLMBackend`, ready for either\n    ``generate`` or ``complete`` calls.\n\nRaises:\n    LLMBackendNotSupportedError: When an unsupported identifier is\n        requested.\n    LLMBackendUnavailableError: When the requested backend cannot\n        be constructed from the current environment (for example,\n        Groq selected with no API key).", "kind": "method", "line": 392, "name": "get_llm_backend", "signature": "def get_llm_backend(config, backend)"}, {"doc": "Build the raw backend for a normalized identifier.\n\nArgs:\n    normalized: Normalized backend identifier.\n    resolved_config: Mapping derived from ``payload.json``.\nReturns:\n    The raw concrete backend the factory would return without\n    the budget wrapper.\nRaises:\n    LLMBackendUnavailableError: When the requested backend cannot\n        be constructed from the current environment.", "kind": "method", "line": 444, "name": "_build_backend", "signature": "def _build_backend(normalized, resolved_config)"}, {"doc": "Return a raw :class:`AIModel` without the budget wrapper.\n\nTests and the CLI command ``llm_budget`` itself use this entry\npoint so the budget proxy never recurses into itself. scope. Defaults\n          to the command/pipeline name when not specified.\n    command: LazyOwn shell command to execute. Mutually exclusive\n             with pipeline.\n    pipeline: Nested pipeline to invoke. Mutually exclusive with\n              command.\n    args: Optional argument string appended after the command.\n    input_from: Template resolved to the args (overrides args when\n                truthy after resolution).\n    validate: Optional ``validate:`` predicate.\n    condition: Optional ``condition:`` template. Falsy ->\n               step is skipped.\n    on_success: Optional follow-up command executed only when this\n                step succeeded. The hook is itself a LazyOwn command\n                name with no args.\n    on_failure: One of stop|continue|skip. Defaults to stop.\n    timeout_s: Per-step timeout.\n    with_inputs: Free-form dict of step-level template values\n                 accessible via ``inputs.X`` inside the same step.", "kind": "class", "line": 107, "name": "PipelineStep", "signature": "class PipelineStep"}, {"doc": "A loaded, schema-validated pipeline document.", "kind": "class", "line": 148, "name": "PipelineSpec", "signature": "class PipelineSpec"}, {"doc": "Outcome of executing a single PipelineStep.", "kind": "class", "line": 159, "name": "StepResult", "signature": "class StepResult"}, {"doc": "Aggregate result returned by PipelineEngine.run.", "kind": "class", "line": 195, "name": "PipelineRun", "signature": "class PipelineRun"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 230, "name": "_now_iso", "signature": "def _now_iso()"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 234, "name": "_new_run_id", "signature": "def _new_run_id()"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 238, "name": "_is_valid_pipeline_name", "signature": "def _is_valid_pipeline_name(name)"}, {"kind": "method", "line": 244, "name": "_load_payload", "signature": "def _load_payload()"}, {"doc": "Resolves ``{{ scope.path.to.value }}`` against a context dict.\n\nSupported lookups:\n  ``previous.<field>`` — most recent non-skipped step result.\n  ``steps.<name>.<field>`` — explicit named step lookup.\n  ``payload.<key>`` — value from payload.json (read at call time).\n  ``inputs.<key>`` — step-level ``with_inputs`` values.\n  ``findings.<key>`` — aggregated derived values across the run.\n\nUnknown paths resolve to empty string; the engine never raises on a\nbad template. Lists are stringified with ``\" \".join`` so they slot\ncleanly into command-line argument strings.", "kind": "class", "line": 256, "name": "TemplateResolver", "signature": "class TemplateResolver"}, {"doc": "Truthy check on a resolved template expression.", "kind": "class", "line": 322, "name": "ConditionEvaluator", "signature": "class ConditionEvaluator"}, {"doc": "Implements the ``validate:`` predicate for one step.\n\nForms:\n  ``ttl=64``       → output must contain the substring \"ttl=64\".\n  ``re:^ttl=\\d+`` → output must match the trailing Python regex.\n  ``empty``        → output trimmed must be empty.\n  ``non_empty``    → output trimmed must be non-empty.", "kind": "class", "line": 337, "name": "StepValidator", "signature": "class StepValidator"}, {"doc": "Per-command output parsers producing structured derived fields.\n\nEach deriver returns a dict of additional keys merged into\n``StepResult.derived``. "d2bc8fbf04b1d4fa", "symbol_count": 25, "symbols": [{"doc": "Immutable tunables consumed by every sanitizer in this module.\n\nDefaults are conservative; the operator can override any value\nby adding the matching key to ``payload.json``. The dataclass\nis frozen so a sanitizer instance can be shared across threads\nwithout locking. Tightening a value never breaks an existing\ncaller because every helper exposes the resulting behaviour as\na sentinel rather than as an exception.", "kind": "class", "line": 37, "name": "SecurityConfig", "signature": "class SecurityConfig"}, {"doc": "Validate HTTP header names and values before transmission.\n\nHeaders crossing a proxy boundary may carry CR, LF or NUL\nbytes that, if forwarded verbatim, allow an upstream to inject\nextra headers or a response body. The sanitizer strips those\nbytes and then enforces an allowlist regex; values failing\nthe allowlist are replaced by an opaque sentinel rather than\nsilently coerced to the empty string so the operator can spot\nabnormal upstream behaviour in proxy logs.", "kind": "class", "line": 101, "name": "HeaderValueSanitizer", "signature": "class HeaderValueSanitizer"}, {"doc": "Resolve untrusted filenames against a fixed base directory.\n\nEvery resolver is bound to one base directory whose realpath\nis computed at construction; subsequent ``resolve`` calls join\nthe validated relative path with that base and reject anything\nthat would escape it after symlink resolution. Because the\nvalidation logic is centralised here, CodeQL data-flow analysis\nconsistently recognises the sanitisation and the same guarantees\napply to every caller that routes through this class.", "kind": "class", "line": 162, "name": "SessionPathResolver", "signature": "class SessionPathResolver"}, {"doc": "Pick the address a server socket should bind to.\n\nThe resolver fails closed: when the operator has not chosen an\naddress, it falls back to the configured loopback rather than\nthe unspecified ``0.0.0.0`` address. The unspecified address is\nreturned only when ``allow_unspecified_bind`` is ``True`` in\n:class:`SecurityConfig`, which gives the operator an explicit,\nauditable opt-in for exposing the C2 on every interface.", "kind": "class", "line": 256, "name": "BindAddressResolver", "signature": "class BindAddressResolver"}, {"doc": "Render shell commands without leaking the supplied credentials.\n\nThe redactor produces two strings from a single template: an\nexecutable form, where the real credentials are substituted in\nplace, and a display form, where every credential placeholder\nand every byte-for-byte occurrence of the credentials is\nreplaced by an opaque sentinel. Callers must use the executable\nform for ``subprocess`` calls and the display form for printing\nor logging.", "kind": "class", "line": 318, "name": "CommandRedactor", "signature": "class CommandRedactor"}, {"doc": "Project arbitrary Python values into a JSON-safe shape.\n\nExceptions, traceback objects and any value that fails JSON\nserialisation are replaced by opaque sentinels rather than\ntheir ``str`` representation, which prevents stack traces,\ninternal file paths and instance attributes from reaching the\nHTTP client. Recursion is bounded by the configured maximum\ndepth and the breadth of every collection is capped so a\nhostile callee cannot exhaust the responder's stack or memory.", "kind": "class", "line": 406, "name": "OutputSanitizer", "signature": "class OutputSanitizer"}, {"doc": "Return a :class:`SecurityConfig` populated from ``payload``.\n\nConvenience entry point so callers do not need to import the\ndataclass directly. ``payload`` is typically the result of\n``utils.load_payload``; when ``None``, the conservative\ndefaults are returned.", "kind": "method", "line": 477, "name": "build_default_config", "signature": "def build_default_config(payload)"}, {"doc": "Build a configuration object from a ``payload.json`` mapping.\n\nUnknown keys are ignored so adding a new tunable in code\ndoes not require an immediate ``payload.json`` migration.\nType-mismatched values are dropped silently because the\npayload file is hand-edited by operators and the framework\nmust remain operational even with a partially valid file.\n\nArgs:\n    payload: A mapping produced by ``json.load`` over\n        ``payload.json`` (or any equivalent dictionary).\n\nReturns:\n    A new, frozen :class:`SecurityConfig` populated from\n    the supplied mapping.", "kind": "method", "line": 68, "name": "from_payload", "signature": "def from_payload(cls, payload)"}, {"doc": "Bind the sanitizer to a configuration instance.\n\nArgs:\n    config: The :class:`SecurityConfig` from which the\n        regex patterns, length limit and sentinel string\n        are read at validation time.", "kind": "method", "line": 115, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, config)"}, {"doc": "Return True iff ``name`` is a syntactically valid header token.\n\nThe check follows RFC 7230 ``token`` grammar via the\nallowlist regex in :class:`SecurityConfig`.", "kind": "method", "line": 129, "name": "is_valid_name", "signature": "def is_valid_name(self, name)"}, {"doc": "Return a header value that cannot smuggle a response split.\n\nThe output is guaranteed to consist solely of printable\nASCII plus the horizontal-tab character, with no CR, LF\nor NUL bytes, and to be no longer than the configured\n``max_header_value_length``. Inputs that are not strings,\nthat become empty after stripping forbidden bytes, or that\nfail the allowlist are replaced by the configured sentinel.", "kind": "method", "line": 139, "name": "sanitize_value", "signature": "def sanitize_value(self, value)"}, {"doc": "Bind the resolver to an absolute, real base directory.\n\nArgs:\n    base_dir: The directory that all resolved paths must\n        stay within after symlink resolution.\n    config: The :class:`SecurityConfig` providing the\n        allowlist regex and depth limits.", "kind": "method", "line": 174, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, base_dir, config)"}, {"doc": "The resolved, absolute base directory.", "kind": "method", "line": 192, "name": "base_dir", "signature": "def base_dir(self)"}, {"doc": "Return ``(absolute, relative)`` for a safe filename.\n\n``relative`` is suitable for ``send_from_directory`` while\n``absolute`` is the realpath after joining and may be used\nfor ``os.path.isfile`` style checks. Returns ``None`` when\nany structural, textual or filesystem check fails so the\ncaller has a single branch to handle every error.", "kind": "method", "line": 196, "name": "resolve", "signature": "def resolve(self, untrusted_name)"}, {"doc": "Return True iff ``untrusted_name`` resolves to an existing file.\n\nThe method swallows :class:`OSError` so the caller never\nobserves filesystem-level errors during an availability\nprobe; missing, denied or unreadable entries all surface\nas ``False``.", "kind": "method", "line": 238, "name": "file_exists", "signature": "def file_exists(self, untrusted_name)"}, {"doc": "Build a resolver with a prioritised list of candidate addresses.\n\nArgs:\n    config: The :class:`SecurityConfig` providing the\n        loopback fallback, the unspecified address literal\n        and the opt-in flag.\n    preferred_addresses: Operator-controlled address\n        candidates evaluated in order. The first value that\n        parses as a valid IPv4 or IPv6 literal wins.", "kind": "method", "line": 269, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, config, preferred_addresses)"}, {"doc": "Return True iff ``candidate`` is a parseable IP literal.", "kind": "method", "line": 285, "name": "_is_well_formed", "signature": "def _is_well_formed(self, candidate)"}, {"doc": "Return the address sockets should bind to.\n\nResolution order:\n\n1. and lateral movement reasoning.\n\nTracks typed relationships between hosts, users, services, and credentials\nand exposes degree-centrality analysis to identify pivot points without\nrequiring an external graph library.\n\nDesign\n------\n- Single Responsibility : graph structure + centrality only; no I/O\n- Open/Closed           : new relation types added as data, not code\n- Thread-safe           : caller (WorldModel) holds its own RLock\n\nCentrality algorithm\n--------------------\nNormalized degree centrality:\n    C(v) = (in_degree(v) + out_degree(v)) / (2 * (N - 1))\n\nA node with high centrality is reachable by and can reach many others —\nan ideal pivot candidate for lateral movement.", "kind": "class", "line": 245, "name": "NetworkGraph", "signature": "class NetworkGraph"}, "class UnifiedOrchestratorSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 3.A — utils.py must not redeclare class Config.\n\nCLAUDE.md §7 documented a long-standing duplicate Config defect.\nOnce removed, the canonical class lives in core.config. This test is\nthe regression guard: if a future change reintroduces a class Config\nline in utils.py the test fails loudly.", "kind": "class", "line": 643, "name": "ConfigDedupeSpec", "signature": "class ConfigDedupeSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 3.B — OrchestrationCommandSet is discovered as active.\n\nDiscovery walks every module under ``cli.commands.*`` via importlib.\nSome of those modules transitively import ``utils.py`` which parses\n``sys.argv`` at import time. Unittest passes ``-v`` which collides\nwith that parser, so the test temporarily neutralises ``sys.argv``\nwhile discovery runs and restores it after.", "kind": "class", "line": 669, "name": "CommandSetActivationSpec", "signature": "class CommandSetActivationSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 3.C — CLAUDE.md §10.4 mandates docstrings on every public symbol.", "kind": "class", "line": 702, "name": "DocstringDisciplineSpec", "signature": "class DocstringDisciplineSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 4.A — Suggestion source degrades when the graph is missing.\n\nQUICKSTART.md and §15a state that the graph is optional. The status\nbar must therefore never raise when ``graphify-out/`` is absent.", "kind": "class", "line": 745, "name": "GraphifyAvailabilitySpec", "signature": "class GraphifyAvailabilitySpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 5 — regression guards for the two live-shell wiring bugs.\n\nBug 1: ``self.__dict__.get('_cmd')`` returns ``None`` because cmd2\n    exposes the shell through a property, not an instance attribute.\n    The OrchestrationCommandSet must use ``self._cmd`` so the bound\n    shell is resolved correctly.\n\nBug 2: ``cmd2.Cmd.register_precmd_hook`` validates that the callable\n    has the exact type annotations ``PrecommandData`` on both the\n    parameter and the return. Hooks built with looser typing are\n    silently rejected and the status bar never updates after install.", "kind": "class", "line": 767, "name": "CmdIntegrationRegressionSpec", "signature": "class CmdIntegrationRegressionSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 6 — behavioural fixes derived from the operator session log.\n\nThree concrete regressions were observed in the live shell:\n\n* The status bar showed ``next: OllamaModel`` — a graph-node class\n  name rather than a command verb. The suggestion source must\n  surface kill-chain / phase-priority verbs.\n* ``[ ... ] ╔══[...]`` rendered on the same physical line as the\n  multi-line custom prompt. The default ``prompt_join`` must place\n  the bar on its own line.\n* ``orchestrate --phase recon 'get ports'`` routed to SWAN with the\n  hardcoded ``exploit_generation`` task_type. The router must score\n  on the goal text only when ``task_type`` is unset, and the daemon\n  must fall back to ``payload.rhost`` for the target.", "kind": "class", "line": 843, "name": "LiveShellBehaviourSpec", "signature": "class LiveShellBehaviourSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 4.B — Default factories produce ready-to-use objects.", "kind": "class", "line": 994, "name": via\nQ-learning-guided routing.  Only active when AUTO_USE_SWAN=1.\n\nSingle Responsibility : MoE/RL expert routing only — no direct execution.\nOpen/Closed           : Extend SwanOrchestrator subclasses; this selector\n                        never changes to support new experts.\nDependency Inversion  : depends on ICommandSelector interface; imports\n                        swan_agent lazily so the daemon starts even without\n                        GROQ_API_KEY present.", "kind": "class", "line": 765, "name": "SWANSelector", "signature": "class SWANSelector(ICommandSelector)"}, {"doc": "Static map fallback — always returns a CommandDecision, never None.\nSelects OS-appropriate commands when the OS is known.\nSingle Responsibility: static fallback map only.", "kind": "class", "line": 842, "name": "FallbackSelector", "signature": "class FallbackSelector(ICommandSelector)"}, {"doc": "Decorator that demotes commands with a poor recent track record.\n\nWraps another :class:`ICommandSelector`. When the wrapped selector\nproposes a command whose recent ``success_rate`` in\n:class:`modules.metrics.MetricsRecorder` is below the configured\nthreshold and whose attempt count clears\n:data:`METRICS_BIAS_MIN_ATTEMPTS`, the decision is dropped (returns\n``None``) so the cascade falls through to the next selector. The\nrejection itself is logged at debug level and broadcast as a\n``METRICS_BIAS_SKIP`` event so operators can audit why the daemon\nsidestepped an otherwise valid recommendation.\n\nThe fallback selector is intentionally left unwrapped at chain\ncomposition time: when every other selector has been filtered, the\ncascade must still converge on *something*.", "kind": "class", "line": 868, "name": "MetricsAwareSelector", "signature": "class MetricsAwareSelector(ICommandSelector)"}, {"doc": "Wrap every non-fallback selector in :class:`MetricsAwareSelector`.\n\nArgs:\n    selectors: Composed selector chain in cascade order. The last\n        selector that ``isinstance(s, FallbackSelector)`` (or the\n        very last entry as a backstop) is left unwrapped so the\n        cascade still converges when every other recommendation\n        has been filtered.\n    enabled: Master switch. When ``False`` the chain is returned\n        unchanged.\n\nReturns:\n    A new list of selectors with metrics-aware decorators applied\n    in front of every wrapped entry. The original list is not\n    mutated.", "kind": "method", "line": 1064, "name": "_wrap_chain_with_metrics_bias", "signature": "def _wrap_chain_with_metrics_bias(selectors, enabled)"}, {"doc": "When credentials exist in payload.json and open services are known,\ngenerates credential-spray commands against those services.\n\nOnly activates in exploit/lateral/privesc/cred phases.\nTracks sprayed (command, target, user) tuples to avoid repeating.\nSingle Responsibility: credential reuse selection only.", "kind": "class", "line": 1102, "name": "CredentialSpraySelector", "signature": "class CredentialSpraySelector(ICommandSelector)"}, {"doc": "Chains selectors in order and returns the first non-None result.\n\nOpen/Closed: extend by adding selectors without modifying existing ones.", "kind": "class", "line": 1158, "name": "CascadeStrategy", "signature": "class CascadeStrategy"}, {"doc": "Decides the next command for a (target, phase) pair.\n\nCascade identical to lazyown_mcp.py auto_loop:\n  1. Every error path is logged through the\nnarrator and reflected in the returned summary so the operator (or the\nMCP caller) sees the full timeline.", "kind": "class", "line": 2550, "name": "EngageOrchestrator", "signature": "class EngageOrchestrator"}, {"doc": "Generate a client-ready report at the end of an auto engagement.\n\nBest-effort: a report failure never fails the engagement, it only\ndowngrades the returned status. The report is a timestamped Markdown\nfile written to ``sessions/`` by ``modules.report_generator``.\n\nReturns:\n    ``{\"generated\": True, \"path\": \"...\"}`` on success or\n    ``{\"generated\": False, \"error\": \"...\"}`` when generation failed.", "kind": "method", "line": 2851, "name": "_maybe_generate_report", "signature": "def _maybe_generate_report()"}, {"doc": "Synchronous helper used by all engage entry points.\n\nArgs:\n    target: IPv4 dotted-quad or hostname to engage.\n    max_switches_per_step: Maximum number of fallback tools per phase.\n    auto: When True the engagement runs fully unattended. rationale forwarded to the operator.\n    target: Active target host the command will run against.\n    proposed_at: Epoch seconds when the action was registered.\n    ttl_seconds: How long the action waits before expiring.\n    decision: One of :data:`DECISION_PENDING`,\n        :data:`DECISION_APPROVED`, :data:`DECISION_VETOED`,\n        :data:`DECISION_EXPIRED`.\n    decided_at: Epoch seconds when the decision was recorded\n        (``0.0`` while pending).\n    operator: Identifier of the operator who decided (empty when\n        expired).", "kind": "class", "line": 51, "name":     :data:`MODE_PAUSED`. Default is auto, which preserves the\n        historical daemon behaviour.\n    vetoed_commands: First-token names the daemon must avoid.\n    focus_targets: When non-empty, the daemon only executes\n        objectives whose target appears in this list.\n    pending: Active approval request, when ``mode == approval`` and\n        the daemon has proposed a command.\n    updated_at: Epoch seconds of the last write — populated by\n        :meth:`DaemonControl.save`.", "kind": "class", "line": 90, "name": "ControlState", "signature": "class ControlState"}, {"doc": "Return the first whitespace-separated token of ``command``.", "kind": "method", "line": 160, "name": "_first_token", "signature": "def _first_token(command)"}, {"doc": "Atomic read/write facade for ``sessions/daemon_control.json``.\n\nAll mutations write to a temp file then ``os.replace`` for\natomicity so concurrent readers (daemon + CLI + MCP) never observe\npartial JSON. ``False`` when\n    ``max_wait_seconds`` elapsed without a resume signal.", "kind": "method", "line": 461, "name": "wait_until_unpaused", "signature": "def wait_until_unpaused(control)"}, {"doc": "Return ``True`` when a still-pending action has exceeded its TTL.", "kind": "method", "line": 81, "name": "is_expired", "signature": "def is_expired(self, now)"}, {"doc": "Serialise the state to a plain JSON-ready dict.", "kind": "method", "line": 112, "name": "to_dict", "signature": "def to_dict(self)"}, {"doc": "Build a state from JSON data, sanitising malformed input.", "kind": "method", "line": 123, "name": "from_dict", "signature": "def from_dict(cls, data)"}, {"doc": "Pin the control file to ``<sessions_dir>/daemon_control.json``.\n\nArgs:\n    sessions_dir: Absolute or relative path to the LazyOwn\n        ``sessions/`` directory. The directory is created on\n        the first write if it does not yet exist.", "kind": "method", "line": 177, "name": "__init__", "signature": "def __init__(self, sessions_dir)"}, {"doc": "Absolute path of the control file on disk.", "kind": "method", "line": 190, "name": "path", "signature": "def path(self)"}, {"doc": "Return the current state or defaults when the file is missing.", "kind": "method", "line": 194, "name": "load", "signature": "def load(self)"}, {"doc": "Persist ``state`` atomically.\n\nThe ``updated_at`` field is overwritten with the current epoch\nso callers do not need to maintain it.", "kind": "method", "line": 207, "name": "save", "signature": "def save(self, state)"}, {"doc": "Switch between :data:`MODE_AUTO`, :data:`MODE_APPROVAL`, :data:`MODE_PAUSED`.", "kind": "method", "line": 237, "name": "set_mode", "signature": "def set_mode(self, mode)"}, {"doc": "Convenience wrapper for ``set_mode(MODE_PAUSED)``.", "kind": "method", "line": 248, "name": "pause", "signature": "def pause(self)"}, {"doc": "Convenience wrapper for ``set_mode(MODE_AUTO)``.", "kind": "method", "line": 252, "name": "resume", "signature": "def resume(self)"}, {"doc": "Convenience wrapper for ``set_mode(MODE_APPROVAL)``.", "kind": "method", "line": 256, "name": "require_approval", "signature": "def require_approval(self)"}, {"doc": "Append a first-token name to the veto list.\n\nRaises:\n    ValueError: When ``command_token`` is empty.", "kind": "method", "line": 260, "name": "add_veto", "signature": "def add_veto(self, command_token)"}, {"doc": "Remove a previously vetoed command from the list.", "kind": "method", "line": 275, "name": "remove_veto", "signature": "def remove_veto(self, command_token)"}, {"doc": "Remove every entry from the veto list.", "kind": "method", "line": 283, "name": "clear_vetoes", "signature": "def clear_vetoes(self)"}, {"doc": "Replace the focus-target list. An empty list disables focus.", "kind": "method", "line": 290, "name": "set_focus", "signature": "def set_focus(self, targets)"}, {"doc": "Daemon-side: register a pending action awaiting approval.\n\nReturns the freshly created :class:`PendingAction` whose\n``action_id`` the daemon will use when calling\n:func:`wait_for_decision` and :meth:`consume`.", "kind": "method", "line": 298, "name": "propose", "signature": "def propose(self, command)"}, {"doc": "Operator-side: approve or veto the pending action.\n\nReturns the updated :class:`PendingAction` or ``None`` when\nthere is no pending action with the supplied id.\n\nRaises:\n    ValueError: When ``decision`` is not approved or vetoed.", "kind": "method", "line": 327, "name": "decide", "signature": "def decide(self, action_id, decision)"}, {"doc": "Daemon-side: read the final decision and clear the slot.\n\nWhen the action is still pending but has exceeded its TTL the\nreturned :class:`PendingAction` carries ``decision =\nDECISION_EXPIRED``. the pending decision\nin real time. Resolution is delegated back to the file sink.", "kind": "class", "line": 1428, "name": "BroadcastApprovalSink", "signature": "class BroadcastApprovalSink(IApprovalSink)"}, {"doc": "Interactive sink that asks the operator on stdin when a TTY is attached.\n\nThe sink only triggers when sys.stdin is a TTY. It writes a prompt,\nreads a single line, and returns the matching ApprovalOutcome.\nFalls back to a pending state when no TTY is available or input fails.", "kind": "class", "line": 1478, "name": "StdinApprovalSink", "signature": "class StdinApprovalSink(IApprovalSink)"}, {"doc": "Fan-out announces to every sink; resolution picks the first answer.\n\nOrder matters: faster channels (stdin) come first so an operator who\nanswers at the prompt resolves the request before the daemon polls\nthe slow file sink.", "kind": "class", "line": 1534, "name": "CompositeApprovalSink", "signature": "class CompositeApprovalSink(IApprovalSink)"}, {"doc": "Human-in-the-loop gate consulted by the EngageOrchestrator.\n\nReads ``payload.json[auto_approve]`` at request time (never cached) so\noperators can flip the value with ``set auto_approve false`` between\nsteps without restarting the daemon.\n\n- auto_approve truthy (default) : every request returns APPROVED.\n- auto_approve false            : requests in gated phases announce\n                                  through the sink and poll up to\n                                  ``poll_seconds`` for a decision. When\n                                  the deadline expires the gate returns\n                                  DENIED so the daemon falls back to a\n                                  safer alternative instead of running\n                                  an unsupervised exploit.\n- phase not in _GATED_CATEGORIES: APPROVED without prompting.\n\nSOLID:\n  S — owns the policy decision only; persistence and notification live\n      in the injected sink.\n  O — gated categories are pulled from ActionCategory + a small string\n      set; extend via a subclass that overrides ``_is_gated``.\n  D — depends on the IApprovalSink interface, not on file or HTTP code.", "kind": "class", "line": 1582, "name": "ApprovalGate", "signature": "class ApprovalGate"}, {"doc": "Thin wrapper around time.sleep for ApprovalGate injection in tests.", "kind": "method", "line": 1695, "name": "_default_sleep", "signature": "def _default_sleep(seconds)"}, {"doc": "Load ``cli/scope_guard.py`` directly from its file path (cached).\n\nThe scope guard is pure standard library, but importing it through the\n``cli`` package triggers ``cli/__init__.py`` which pulls the full cmd2\ncommand stack. Loading the module file in isolation keeps this gate\ndependency-light and side-effect free. The loaded module is registered\nin ``sys.modules`` before execution so ``@dataclass`` under\n``from __future__ import annotations`` can resolve its own type\nnamespace, and the result is cached across calls.\n\nReturns:\n    The loaded ``scope_guard`` module.\n\nRaises:\n    ImportError: When the module spec or loader cannot be built.\n    OSError: When the module file cannot be read.", "kind": "method", "line": 1712, "name": "_load_scope_guard", "signature": "def _load_scope_guard()"}, {"doc": "Return whether *target* is inside *entries*, failing closed on error.\n\nBacked by ``cli.scope_guard.target_in_scope`` loaded in isolation. When\nthe scope guard cannot be loaded the predicate returns ``False`` so an\nunverifiable scope check denies an out-of-scope step under ``enforce``\nrather than attacking an unauthorized host.\n\nArgs:\n    target: The active target (IP address or hostname).\n    entries: Normalized authorized scope entries.\n\nReturns:\n    ``True`` when the target is authorized by at least one entry.", "kind": "method", "line": 1752, "name": "_default_in_scope", "signature": "def _default_in_scope(target, entries)"}, {"doc": "Normalize raw payload scope entries into a clean tuple.\n\nDelegates to ``cli.scope_guard.normalize_scope`` and falls back to a\nconservative string strip when the guard cannot be loaded.\n\nArgs:\n    entries: Raw ``payload.json[scope]`` value (typically a list).\n\nReturns:\n    A tuple of non-empty, stripped scope entries.", "kind": "method", "line": 1773, "name": "_normalize_scope", "signature": "def _normalize_scope(entries)"}, {"doc": "Headless approval gate backing the fully autonomous engage mode.\n\nDrop-in replacement for :class:`ApprovalGate` that never blocks on a\nhuman decision. Every request resolves immediately from the authorized\nscope declared in ``payload.json``:\n\n- scope empty OR ``scope_enforcement`` is ``off`` : APPROVED. The scope\n  guard is dormant, so unattended autonomy runs unconstrained.\n- target inside scope                             : APPROVED.\n- target outside scope, enforcement ``warn``      : APPROVED, with a\n  rationale flagging the out-of-scope target for the narrator/audit log.\n- target outside scope, enforcement ``enforce``   : DENIED. This is the\n  single fail-closed boundary unattended autonomy must keep — the\n  engagement's legal authorization limit.\n\nThe payload is read at request time (never cached) so an operator can\ntighten scope with ``scope enforce`` mid-run and have the next step\nhonour it.\n\nSOLID:\n  S — owns only the scope-versus-target decision; no I/O beyond reading\n      the payload it is configured with.\n  L — honours the same ``request`` signature and ``ApprovalOutcome``\n      return type as :class:`ApprovalGate`, so ``EngageOrchestrator``\n      consumes either interchangeably.\n  D — the scope predicate is injected via ``in_scope_fn`` so the gate is\n      unit-testable without loading ``cli.scope_guard``.", "kind": "class", "line": 1793, "name": "ScopeBoundAutoGate", "signature": "class ScopeBoundAutoGate"}, {"doc": "One-shot importer that reads LazyOwn_session_report.csv and populates\nthe episode store and transition table from historical session data.", "kind": canonical class lives in core.config. This test is\nthe regression guard: if a future change reintroduces a class Config\nline in utils.py the test fails loudly.", "kind": "class", "line": 643, "name": "ConfigDedupeSpec", "signature": "class ConfigDedupeSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 3.B — OrchestrationCommandSet is discovered as active.\n\nDiscovery walks every module under ``cli.commands.*`` via importlib.\nSome of those modules transitively import ``utils.py`` which parses\n``sys.argv`` at import time. Unittest passes ``-v`` which collides\nwith that parser, so the test temporarily neutralises ``sys.argv``\nwhile discovery runs and restores it after.", "kind": "class", "line": 669, "name": "CommandSetActivationSpec", "signature": "class CommandSetActivationSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 3.C — CLAUDE.md §10.4 mandates docstrings on every public symbol.", "kind": "class", "line": 702, "name": "DocstringDisciplineSpec", "signature": "class DocstringDisciplineSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 4.A — Suggestion source degrades when the graph is missing.\n\nQUICKSTART.md and §15a state that the graph is optional. The status\nbar must therefore never raise when ``graphify-out/`` is absent.", "kind": "class", "line": 745, "name": "GraphifyAvailabilitySpec", "signature": "class GraphifyAvailabilitySpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 5 — regression guards for the two live-shell wiring bugs.\n\nBug 1: ``self.__dict__.get('_cmd')`` returns ``None`` because cmd2\n    exposes the shell through a property, not an instance attribute.\n    The OrchestrationCommandSet must use ``self._cmd`` so the bound\n    shell is resolved correctly.\n\nBug 2: ``cmd2.Cmd.register_precmd_hook`` validates that the callable\n    has the exact type annotations ``PrecommandData`` on both the\n    parameter and the return. Hooks built with looser typing are\n    silently rejected and the status bar never updates after install.", "kind": "class", "line": 767, "name": "CmdIntegrationRegressionSpec", "signature": "class CmdIntegrationRegressionSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 6 — behavioural fixes derived from the operator session log.\n\nThree concrete regressions were observed in the live shell:\n\n* The status bar showed ``next: OllamaModel`` — a graph-node class\n  name rather than a command verb. The suggestion source must\n  surface kill-chain / phase-priority verbs.\n* ``[ ... ] ╔══[...]`` rendered on the same physical line as the\n  multi-line custom prompt. The default ``prompt_join`` must place\n  the bar on its own line.\n* ``orchestrate --phase recon 'get ports'`` routed to SWAN with the\n  hardcoded ``exploit_generation`` task_type. The router must score\n  on the goal text only when ``task_type`` is unset, and the daemon\n  must fall back to ``payload.rhost`` for the target.", "kind": "class", "line": 843, "name": "LiveShellBehaviourSpec", "signature": "class LiveShellBehaviourSpec(TestCase)"}, {"doc": "Spec 4.B — Default factories produce ready-to-use objects.", "kind": "class", "line": 994, "name": input string using a regular expression.\n\nThe input string is expected to be in the format: 'IP: (192.168.1.222) MAC: ec:c3:02:b0:4c:96'.\nThe function uses a regular expression to match and extract the IP address and MAC address from the input.\n\nArgs:\n    input_string (str): The formatted string containing the IP and MAC addresses.\n\nReturns:\n    tuple: A tuple containing the extracted IP address and MAC address. If the format is incorrect, returns (None, None).", "kind": "function", "line": 291, "name": "parse_ip_mac", "signature": "def parse_ip_mac(input_string)"}, {"doc": "Constructs an ARP packet with the given source and destination IP and MAC addresses.\n\nThe function creates both Ethernet and ARP headers, combining them into a complete ARP packet.\n\nArgs:\n    src_mac (str): Source MAC address in the format 'xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx'.\n    src_ip (str): Source IP address in dotted decimal format (e.g., '192.168.1.1').\n    dst_ip (str): Destination IP address in dotted decimal format (e.g., '192.168.1.2').\n    dst_mac (str): Destination MAC address in the format 'xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx'.\n\nReturns:\n    bytes: The constructed ARP packet containing the Ethernet and ARP headers.", "kind": "function", "line": 313, "name": "create_arp_packet", "signature": "def create_arp_packet(src_mac, src_ip, dst_ip, dst_mac)"}, {"doc": "Sends a raw ARP packet over the specified network interface.\n\nThe function creates a raw socket, binds it to the specified network interface, and sends the given packet.\n\nArgs:\n    packet (bytes): The ARP packet to be sent.\n    iface (str): The name of the network interface to use for sending the packet (e.g., 'eth0').\n\nRaises:\n    OSError: If an error occurs while creating the socket or sending the packet.", "kind": "function", "line": 350, "name": "send_packet", "signature": "def send_packet(packet, iface)"}, {"doc": "Load the version number from the 'version.json' file.\n\nThis function attempts to open the 'version.json' file and load its contents.\nIf the file is found, it retrieves the version number from the JSON data.\nIf the version key does not exist, it returns a default version 'release/v0.0.14'.\nIf the file is not found, it also returns the default version.\n\nThe version.json is the single source of truth, updated by deploy.sh.\n\nReturns:\n- str: The version number from the file or the default version if the file is not found or the version key is missing.", "kind": "function", "line": 367, "name": "load_version", "signature": "def load_version()"}, {"doc": "Interpret a configuration value as a boolean.\n\nAccepts the canonical truthy strings used across payload.json and\nform surfaces (``true``, ``1``, ``yes``, ``on``, case-insensitive).\nAnything else evaluates to False so a missing or typo'd flag can\nnever silently enable a feature.\n\nArgs:\n    value: The raw value; converted to string before inspection.\n\nReturns:\n    bool: True only for the canonical truthy strings.", "kind": "function", "line": 392, "name": "parse_bool", "signature": "def parse_bool(value)"}, {"doc": "Handles signals such as Control + C and shows a message on how to exit.\n\nThis function is used to handle signals like Control + C (SIGINT) and prints\na warning message instructing the user on how to exit the program using the\ncommands 'exit', 'q', or 'qa'.\n\n:param sig: The signal number.\n:type sig: int\n:param frame: The current stack frame.\n:type frame: frame\n:return: None", "kind": "function", "line": 410, "name": "signal_handler", "signature": "def signal_handler(sig, frame)"}, {"doc": "Activates a virtual environment and starts an interactive shell.\n\nThis function activates a virtual environment located at `venv_path` and then\nlaunches an interactive bash shell with the virtual environment activated.\n\n:param venv_path: The path to the virtual environment directory.\n:type venv_path: str\n:return: None", "kind": "function", "line": 437, "name": "activate_virtualenv", "signature": "def activate_virtualenv(venv_path)"}, {"doc": "Internal function to parse a /proc/net file and extract network ports.\n\nThis function reads a file specified by `file_path`, processes each line to\nextract local addresses and ports, and converts them from hexadecimal to decimal.\nThe IP addresses are converted from hexadecimal format to standard dot-decimal\nnotation. The function returns a list of tuples, each containing an IP address\nand a port number.\n\n:param file_path: The path to the /proc/net file to be parsed.\n:type file_path: str\n:return: A list of tuples, each containing an IP address and a port number.\n:rtype: list of tuple", "kind": "function", "line": 462, "name": "parse_proc_net_file", "signature": "def parse_proc_net_file(file_path)"}, {"doc": "Internal function to get open TCP and UDP ports on the operating system.\n\nThis function uses the `parse_proc_net_file` function to extract open TCP and UDP\nports from the corresponding /proc/net files. It returns two lists: one for TCP\nports and one for UDP ports.\n\n:return: A tuple containing two lists: the first list with open TCP ports and\n        the second list with open UDP ports.\n:rtype: tuple of (list of tuple, list of tuple)", "kind": "function", "line": 506, "name": "get_open_ports", "signature": "def get_open_ports()"}, {"doc": "Searches for potential credentials in files within the specified directory.\n\nThis function uses a regular expression to find possible credentials such as\npasswords, secrets, API keys, and tokens in files within the given directory.\nIt iterates through all files in the directory and prints any matches found.\n\n:param directory: The directory to search for files containing credentials.\n:type directory: str\n:return: None", "kind": "function", "line": 525, "name": "find_credentials", "signature": "def find_credentials(directory)"}, {"doc": "Internal function to rotate characters for ROT cipher.\n\nThis function takes a character and a shift value, and rotates the character\nby the specified shift amount. It only affects alphabetical characters, leaving\nnon-alphabetical characters unchanged.\n\n:param c: The character to be rotated.\n:type c: str\n:param shift: The number of positions to shift the character.\n:type shift: int\n:return: The rotated character.\n:rtype: str", "kind": "function", "line": 557, "name": "rotate_char", "signature": "def rotate_char(c, shift)"}, {"doc": "Retrieves network interface information with their associated IP addresses.\n\nThis function executes a shell command to gather network interface details,\nparses the output to extract interface names and their corresponding IP addresses,\nand returns this information in a dictionary format. The dictionary keys are\ninterface names, and the values are IP addresses.\n\n:return: A dictionary where the keys are network interface names and the values\n         are their associated IP addresses.\n:rtype: dict", "kind": "function", "line": 578, "name": "get_network_info", "signature": "def get_network_info()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 611, "name": "get_git_info", "signature": "def get_git_info()"}, {"kind": "function", "line": 625, "name": "get_venv_info", "signature": "def get_venv_info()"}, {"doc": "Read ``payload.json`` defensively for the prompt renderer.\n\nThe prompt is rendered before the shell finishes wiring its parameters,\nso direct attribute access on the shell would race. Reading the file\neach time keeps the prompt in sync with operator-driven updates without\ncoupling the renderer to the shell's lifecycle.", "kind": "function", "line": 631, "name": "_load_prompt_payload", "signature": "def _load_prompt_payload()"}, {"doc": "Render the configurable Neon Box prompt for the cmd2 shell.\n\nDelegates to :func:`cli.banner_config.render_prompt` so the entire\nsegment registry, color palette, and toggling logic live in a single\nself-contained module. Failure to import the renderer falls back to a\nminimal single-line prompt so the shell stays usable.\n\nReturns:\n    str: The fully styled multi-line prompt string ready for cmd2.", "kind": "function", "line": 645, "name": "getprompt", "signature": "def getprompt()"}, {"doc": "Copia el texto proporcionado al portapapeles usando xclip.\n\nArgs:\n    text (str): El texto que se desea copiar al portapapeles.\n\nExample:\n    copy2clip(\"Hello, World!\")", "kind": "function", "line": 662, "name": "copy2clip", "signature": "def copy2clip(text)"}, {"doc": "Removes color escape sequences and other non-printable characters.", "kind": "function", "line": 681, "name": "clean_output", "signature": "def clean_output(output)"}, {"doc": "Processes a file to extract and display characters from specific write sequences.\n\nArgs:\n    filename (str): El nombre del archivo a leer.\n\nRaises:\n    FileNotFoundError: Si el archivo no se encuentra.\n    Exception: Para otros errores que puedan ocurrir.", "kind": "function", "line": 693, "name": "teclado_usuario", "signature": "def teclado_usuario(filename)"}, {"doc": "Lee un archivo, extrae texto desde secuencias de escritura y muestra el contenido reconstruido.\n\nArgs:\n    filename (str): El nombre del archivo a leer.\n\nRaises:\n    FileNotFoundError: Si el archivo no se encuentra.\n    Exception: Para otros errores que puedan ocurrir.", "kind": "function", "line": 730, "name": "salida_strace", "signature": "def salida_strace(filename)"}, {"doc": "Process and display results from ExploitAlert.\n\nThis function checks if the provided content contains any results.\nIf results are present, it prints the title and link for each exploit found,\nand appends the results to a predata list. If no results are found,\nit prints an error message.\n\nParameters:\n- content (list): A list of dictionaries containing exploit information.\n\nReturns:\nNone\nThanks to Sicat 🐈\nAn excellent tool for CVE detection, I implemented only the keyword search as I had to change some libraries. **Methods:**
- `_substitute` (line 42) `def _substitute(template, payload)` - *Render ``template`` against ``payload`` placeholders.

Falls back to the literal template if ``str.format_map`` raises
(e.g. unbalanced braces from legacy strings) so a malformed entry
cannot prevent the shell from booting.*
- `template_placeholders` (line 56) `def template_placeholders(template)` - *Return the ``{name}`` placeholders referenced by ``template``.

Malformed templates (unbalanced braces from legacy strings) yield an
empty set — the same fail-safe spirit as :func:`_substitute`.*
- `empty_placeholders` (line 72) `def empty_placeholders(template, context)` - *Return placeholders whose rendered value against ``context`` is empty.*
- `load_aliases` (line 77) `def load_aliases(payload, path, lazy)` - *Return the cmd2 alias map.

Args:
    payload: Configuration dict for placeholder substitution. Used only
        when ``lazy=False``. If ``None`` the function reads
        ``payload.json`` lazily so callers don't have to import
        :mod:`core.config` themselves.
    path: Override the YAML location (used by tests).
    lazy: When ``True`` (default), preserve ``{name}`` placeholders so
        ``LazyOwnShell.onecmd_plus_hooks`` can re-render them against the
        *current* params at execution time — meaning ``set rhost X``
        instantly updates every alias that references ``{rhost}``. Pass
        ``lazy=False`` for the legacy snapshot behaviour.

Returns:
    Flat ``{name: command}`` dict suitable for ``self.aliases.update(...)``.

Raises:
    FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
    yaml.YAMLError: file is malformed YAML.
    TypeError: top-level YAML is not a mapping.
    ValueError: a key or value has the wrong type.*

#### `assign.py`
**Path:** `cli/assign.py`

**Functions:**
- `apply_assign` (line 36) `def apply_assign(params, key, value)` - *Validate, mutate and persist a single payload assignment.

Args:
    params: Live parameter dict. Mutated in place when ``key`` exists.
    key: Parameter name.
    value: New value to store.
    save: Optional callable invoked with ``params`` after a successful
        mutation. Pass :func:`core.config.save_payload` to persist to
        ``payload.json``. ``None`` skips persistence (useful for tests).
    on_issue: Optional callback invoked with the validation issue when
        the value fails the schema for ``key``. The assignment still
        proceeds — the callback exists only so the caller (typically
        the CLI) can surface a hint to the operator.

Returns:
    ``True`` if ``key`` existed in ``params`` and was updated;
    ``False`` otherwise. Callers can use the return value to decide
    whether to refresh dependent state (e.g. aliases).*

The provider tries:
1. ``modules.cli_auth.get_current_operator()`` for username,
   then reads the operator's stored credential hash from ``users.json``.
2. Falls back to ``LAZYOWN_MASTER_PASSWORD`` environment variable.
3. Returns None when no credential is available (crypto is skipped).

Returns:
    A zero-argument callable returning the operator's password or None.*

#### `autosuggest.py`
**Path:** `cli/autosuggest.py`

**Classes:**
- `SuggestionContext` (line 50) `class SuggestionContext` - *Inputs available to every suggestion provider.

Args:
    last_command: First token of the last command executed.
    phase: Current engagement phase (recon, enum, exploit, ...).
    recent_commands: Last N commands from the session transcript,
        newest entries appearing last.
    target: Active rhost loaded from ``payload.json``.
    os_hint: Detected target OS — ``"linux"``, ``"windows"``, or
        ``"unknown"``.*
- `Suggestion` (line 71) `class Suggestion` - *One next-command suggestion with its rationale.

Args:
    command: Shell command executed when the operator accepts the
        suggestion via ``do_next``.
    reason: Human-readable explanation surfaced in the prompt and
        event log.
    score: Provider-specific confidence. Higher is better. The
        :class:`CompositeProvider` uses it to arbitrate across
        providers.
    source: Short label identifying which provider produced the
        suggestion (``graph``, ``killchain``, ``phase``, ...).*
- `SuggestionProvider` (line 92) `class SuggestionProvider(Protocol)` - *Provider contract: examine context, return one suggestion or ``None``.*
- `CompositeProvider` (line 98) `class CompositeProvider` - *Aggregator that returns the highest-scoring suggestion across providers.

Adding a provider is a constructor argument; the engine itself
never changes, honouring the Open/Closed principle.*
- `KillChainProvider` (line 134) `class KillChainProvider` - *Provider backed by the static kill-chain adjacency map.

Falls back to the phase-priority table when no adjacency entry
exists for the last command. Commands already present in
:attr:`SuggestionContext.recent_commands` are skipped so the
suggestion is always forward-looking.*
- `GraphProvider` (line 189) `class GraphProvider` - *Provider backed by the graphify knowledge-graph advisor.

Accepts any object exposing ``suggest_next(recent_commands, limit)``
returning a list of dicts so this module stays decoupled from the
concrete :class:`cli.graph_advisor.GraphAdvisor` implementation.*
- `AutoSuggestEngine` (line 245) `class AutoSuggestEngine` - *Stateful holder for the active ghost-text suggestion.

The engine is a thin coordinator: it never decides what to suggest
(delegated to its :class:`SuggestionProvider`) and only owns the
current-suggestion state machine plus the rendering surface for the
prompt.*

**Methods:**
- `_truncate` (line 335) `def _truncate(value, max_len)` - *Return ``value`` shortened to ``max_len`` characters with an ellipsis.*
- `format_hint_line` (line 344) `def format_hint_line(suggestion)` - *Build the dim hint string surfaced after each command.

The format is deliberately compact and unambiguous about the
accept key: ``  >> press '.' to run: gobuster (reason via graph)``.
Truncation honours :data:`HINT_COMMAND_LIMIT` and
:data:`HINT_REASON_LIMIT` so the line never exceeds one terminal
row at the typical 100-column width.

Args:
    suggestion: Suggestion to render.
    accept_key: Visible key the operator presses to accept.
    command_limit: Maximum command-fragment length.
    reason_limit: Maximum reason-fragment length.

Returns:
    Plain string (no ANSI). The shell wraps it in dim style at
    render time so callers can pipe the value into logs without
    carrying escape codes.*
- `render_hint_line` (line 377) `def render_hint_line(engine)` - *Print one dim hint line for the engine's active suggestion.

Returns ``True`` when something was printed, ``False`` otherwise.
The function is a no-op when the engine is disabled or has no
active suggestion so callers can register it unconditionally as a
cmd2 postcmd hook.

Args:
    engine: :class:`AutoSuggestEngine` whose current suggestion to
        render.
    console: Optional ``rich.console.Console`` instance. When
        ``None`` a module-private console is used so tests can
        inject a capturing console.
    prefix: Leading marker, default matches ``cli.reactive_hints``.
    accept_key: Visible accept-key hint passed through to
        :func:`format_hint_line`.*
- `_hint_console` (line 413) `def _hint_console()` - *Return a lazily-initialised :class:`rich.console.Console`.

Imported lazily so unit tests can run without ``rich`` installed.
The instance is cached at module scope so subsequent calls reuse
the same console.*
- `build_default_engine` (line 429) `def build_default_engine(advisor, chain, phase_priority)` - *Wire the canonical provider chain used by the cmd2 shell.

Order is: graph provider (high signal) followed by the kill-chain

#### `_base.py`
**Path:** `cli/commands/_base.py`

**Classes:**
- `LazyOwnCommandSet` (line 32) `class LazyOwnCommandSet(CommandSet)` - *Base class for every phase ``CommandSet`` defined under ``cli.commands``.

Attributes:
    phase: Kill-chain phase identifier (``recon``, ``enum``, ...). Used
        by tooling such as ``lazyown_phase_guide`` and the autonomous
        daemon to filter commands by phase.
    category: cmd2 help category label. Defaults to a Title-Case form
        of ``phase`` when not set explicitly.*

**Methods:**
- `_resolve_shell` (line 46) `def _resolve_shell(self)` - *Return the bound parent shell, or ``None`` before registration.

``cmd2`` stores the parent shell in a name-mangled private attribute
and exposes it through the :attr:`cmd2.CommandSet._cmd` property, which
raises :class:`CommandSetRegistrationError` until the set is
registered. This helper centralises that access so the migrated
``do_*`` methods can forward attribute reads without leaking the cmd2
registration exception or depending on cmd2 internals.

Returns:
    The parent ``LazyOwnShell`` instance once the set is registered,
    otherwise ``None``.*
- `params` (line 67) `def params(self)` - *Return the live ``params`` dict owned by the parent shell.

Returns:
    The same dict object that ``LazyOwnShell.params`` exposes when
    the set is registered, or an empty dict when it is not.*
- `payload` (line 78) `def payload(self)` - *Return the parent shell's ``Config`` wrapper when available.

Returns:
    ``LazyOwnShell.config`` when the shell publishes it, otherwise
    ``LazyOwnShell.params`` so callers always receive a mapping-
    like object. Falls back to an empty dict before registration.*
- `__getattr__` (line 91) `def __getattr__(self, name)` - *Forward unknown attribute access to the bound shell or utils.

``cmd2`` binds the parent shell to ``self._cmd`` when the
``CommandSet`` is registered. Migrated methods reference shell
state directly (``self.run_script``, ``self.c2_url``, ...) so this
forwarder lets them execute unmodified once they are wired in.

Migrated ``do_*`` methods also call single-underscore shell helpers
that stayed on ``LazyOwnShell`` (``self._scope_save``,
``self._load_adversaries``, ``self._payload_factory``, ...). Those
are forwarded to the bound shell as well; only dunder names and
``complete_*`` completion probes are refused outright, because
forwarding them would leak Python/cmd2 machinery. Private names are
never resolved from ``utils`` — a private helper only ever lives on
the shell.

When a public name is not on the shell, the forwarder falls back to
the ``utils`` module namespace, giving migrated CommandSets access
to every re-exported symbol (``os``, ``json``, ``glob``,
``getprompt``, category constants, etc.) without per-file import
boilerplate.

Args:
    name: Attribute name requested by the caller.

Returns:
    The attribute value resolved on the bound shell or utils.

Raises:
    AttributeError: When ``name`` is a dunder or ``complete_*``
        probe, when the shell is not yet bound (inert before
        registration), or when neither the shell nor ``utils``
        expose a public ``name``.*

#### `_dormancy.py`
**Path:** `cli/commands/_dormancy.py`

**Classes:**
- `PendingCommandSet` (line 30) `class PendingCommandSet(LazyOwnCommandSet)` - *Base class for migrated-but-not-yet-active phase command sets.

Subclasses are discovered by :func:`cli.registry.iter_command_sets` but
excluded from :func:`cli.registry.register_command_sets`, so the
framework boots without colliding with the equivalent ``do_*`` methods
still defined on :class:`LazyOwnShell`.

Activation procedure:
    1. Remove the equivalent ``do_*`` methods from ``lazyown.py``.
    2. Change the subclass base from :class:`PendingCommandSet` to
       :class:`LazyOwnCommandSet`.
    3. Restart the shell (``./run``) or the MCP server
       (``bash skills/mcp_restart.sh``).

The marker is read via ``getattr(cls, '__lazyown_pending__', False)``
so non-marker subclasses always opt out by absence.*

**Methods:**
- `is_pending` (line 52) `def is_pending(cs_class)` - *Return ``True`` when ``cs_class`` is flagged as a pending migration.

Args:
    cs_class: A ``CommandSet`` subclass discovered by the registry.

Returns:
    ``True`` when the class declares ``__lazyown_pending__ = True``,
    either directly or through inheritance from :class:`PendingCommandSet`.
    ``False`` for active sets and for non-class inputs.*

1. If no arguments are provided:
    - Retrieves the target IP (`self.params['rhost']`) from parameters.
    - Checks if the IP is valid using `check_rhost()`. If invalid, exits the function.
    - Creates a Metasploit resource script (`/tmp/scan_vulnerabilities.rc`) that includes commands for scanning ports, enumerating services, and checking for known vulnerabilities.
    - Executes Metasploit with the created resource script and then deletes the temporary file.
    - Prints a shutdown message after running the scan.

2. If the argument starts with "rev":
    - Sets up a reverse shell payload based on the specified platform and user choice (with or without meterpreter).
    - Creates a Metasploit resource script (`/tmp/handler.rc`) for handling incoming reverse shell connections.
    - Executes Metasploit with the created resource script and then deletes the temporary file.
    - Prints a shutdown message after setting up the handler.

3. If the argument starts with "lnk":
    - Configures parameters (`self.params['lhost']`, `lport`) for creating a payload.
    - Uses `msfvenom` to generate a payload executable and saves it in the `sessions` directory.
    - Creates an XML file (`download_payload.xml`) that will be used to download and execute the payload on a target machine.
    - Creates a PowerShell script (`create_lnk.ps1`) to generate a shortcut file (`.lnk`) pointing to the payload.
    - Prints instructions and generates a command to copy to the clipboard for setting up the payload and files.

4. If the argument starts with "autoroute":
    - Configures parameters for setting up a Metasploit session and autorouting.
    - Creates a Metasploit resource script (`/tmp/autoroute.rc`) to handle exploit sessions and assign up autorouting.
    - Executes Metasploit with the resource script and starts a SOCKS proxy for routing traffic.
    - Configures proxychains to use the Metasploit SOCKS proxy and prints instructions for using proxychains with tools.

:param line: The command line input that determines which Metasploit task to automate.
:type line: str
:returns: None

Manual execution:
To manually run these tasks, you would need to:
- For scanning: Create and run the resource script using `msfconsole -r /tmp/scan_vulnerabilities.rc`.
- For reverse shells: Configure and run the resource script with the appropriate payload settings.
- For payload generation and shortcuts: Use `msfvenom` and create XML and PowerShell scripts as specified.

- `do_smbmap` (line 225) `def do_smbmap(self, line)` - *smbmap -H 10.10.10.3 [OPTIONS]
Uses the `smbmap` tool to interact with SMB shares on a remote host:

1. Checks if `rhost` (remote host) and `lhost` (local host) are assign; if not, an error message is displayed.
2. If no `line` (share name or options) is provided:
- Attempts to access SMB shares on the remote host with a default user `deefbeef` using the command: `smbmap -H {rhost} -u 'deefbeef'`
3. If `line` is provided:
- Executes `smbmap` with the specified options or share name using the command: `smbmap -H {rhost} -R {line}`
4. Suggests a potential SMB exploit if possible by mounting the share from the local host using: `mount -t cifs "//{lhost}/documents" /mnt/smb`

:param line: Options or share name to use with `smbmap`. If not provided, uses a default user to list shares.

- `do_estorides_loop` (line 319) `def do_estorides_loop(self, line)` - *Run the bidirectional Estorides <-> LazyOwn feedback loop.

Each iteration:
  1. Extract seeds from LazyOwn (world model, scope, DB, hosts files)
  2. Feed each seed into Estorides discover for passive OSINT
  3. Import new entities back into LazyOwn DB + scope
  4. New entities become seeds for the next iteration
  5. Runs lazynmap / nuclei if operator opts in on new targets

The loop converges when no new assets are discovered or max
iterations is reached.

Usage:
    estorides_loop [--iter <n>] [--depth <n>] [--auto-scan]

Options:
    --iter <n>       Max iterations (default: 3)
    --depth <n>      Discovery depth per seed (default: 2)
    --auto-scan      Automatically run lazynmap on new IPs discovered
                     by Estorides (requires active scanning permission)

Examples:
    estorides_loop                    # 3 iterations, passive only
    estorides_loop --iter 5 --depth 3 # 5 iterations, deeper discovery
    estorides_loop --auto-scan        # auto-scan new IPs from OSINT*

- `do_engage` (line 1530) `def do_engage(self, line)` - *Drive a single target through the full kill-chain in one command.

Usage:
    engage <target>                  Run synchronously on the target IP
    engage <target> --auto           Full auto mode: no human in the loop
    engage <target> --background     Detach into a background worker
    engage <target> --max-switches N Set per-step fallback retry limit
    engage --status                  Tail the engagement log + show pending approvals
    engage --pending                 List approval requests awaiting an operator
    engage --approve <id> [--operator name]
    engage --deny <id>    [--operator name]

The orchestrator runs ping/OS detect -> nmap -> auto_populate -> enum
-> exploit-search -> initial-access against the target. Each phase
consults the ApprovalGate when ``auto_approve`` is false in
``payload.json``; gated phases pause for an operator decision before
executing. Failures auto-switch to the next bridge-catalog
alternative. Every action is narrated to ``sessions/engagement.log``
and broadcast through ``modules.collab_bp`` so connected teammates
see the kill-chain in real time.

With ``--auto`` the engagement runs with no human in the loop. The
ApprovalGate is replaced by a ``ScopeBoundAutoGate`` that never
prompts: it approves every step whose target is inside the authorized
``scope`` (or when the scope guard is dormant) and denies any
out-of-scope target while ``scope_enforcement`` is ``enforce`` — the
single fail-closed boundary unattended autonomy keeps. When the
kill-chain finishes a client-ready report is written to ``sessions/``.

:return: None*

Dependencies:
- The function relies on `awk`, `grep`, `cut`, and `xclip` to process and copy the IP address.

Example:
    ip
    # This will display IP addresses for all network interfaces and copy the IP address from `tun0` to the clipboard.

This function performs the following actions:

2. Checks if the `self.params['rhost']` is valid using the `check_rhost` function.

The engagement telemetry must never score input-line noise: menu
selections (``1``), quoted script paths, mistyped emails, host names,
hyphenated or capitalised tokens, or empty input. This conservative
syntactic filter rejects all of those.

It deliberately does **not** consult the static command index: that index
can lag behind the live shell, so gating on it would silently drop real
commands. The authoritative membership test lives in the shell post-command
hook, which checks the token against the live registry via
``get_all_commands()`` before ever calling in. This function is the
module-level safety net for direct callers and historical sanitisation.

Args:
    cmd: Candidate command name, with or without the ``do_`` prefix.

Returns:

This heals persisted state: an entry is kept only when it is syntactically
a command and, when an authoritative ``known`` roster is supplied, is a
member of it. Duplicates are collapsed preserving first-seen order.

Args:

    known: Optional authoritative set of ``do_``-prefixed command names

- `_phase_from_event` (line 48) `def _phase_from_event(event)` - *Return the phase an event belongs to, empty string if absent.*
- `_detect_current_phase` (line 58) `def _detect_current_phase(events, world, phase_keys)` - *Resolve the active phase from events, falling back to the world model.

Args:

    world: Parsed ``world_model.json`` snapshot.
    phase_keys: Ordered list of canonical phase identifiers.

Returns:
    The active phase identifier, or an empty string when unknown.*
- `compute_killchain` (line 83) `def compute_killchain(events, world, phases)` - *Compute kill-chain progress from daemon events and the world model.

A phase is marked *done* when the engagement has advanced past it (its index
is below the active phase) or the world model explicitly lists it as
completed. The active phase is *active*; everything after it is *pending*.
Per-phase activity counts and accumulated reward are derived from the step
events regardless of state.

Args:
    events: Daemon events ordered oldest first (see
        :func:`cli.reasoning_stream.read_raw_events`).
    world: Optional ``world_model.json`` snapshot used as a fallback for the
        current phase and for an explicit ``completed_phases`` list.
    phases: Ordered ``(key, label)`` pairs describing the kill chain.

Returns:
    One :class:`PhaseProgress` per phase, in kill-chain order.*

The defaults below are the only place where palette UX strings,

- `PaletteArgs` (line 125) `class PaletteArgs` - *Parsed result of a single ``palette`` invocation.*
- `PaletteArgumentParser` (line 134) `class PaletteArgumentParser` - *Translate a raw command line into :class:`PaletteArgs`.

Routing rules (deterministic, in declaration order):

1. No tokens: :attr:`PaletteMode.OVERVIEW`.
2. ``--search <query>`` flag: :attr:`PaletteMode.SEARCH`.
3. ``--info <name>`` flag: :attr:`PaletteMode.DETAIL`.
4. Single token that matches a known phase: :attr:`PaletteMode.PHASE`.
5. Single token that does not match a phase: :attr:`PaletteMode.SEARCH`
   with the token as ``query``.
6. Two tokens with first matching a known phase: :attr:`PaletteMode.PHASE`
   with the second token as ``query``.
7. Anything else: :attr:`PaletteMode.OVERVIEW` (the renderer falls back
   to a help-style listing).*
- `PaletteIndexQuery` (line 186) `class PaletteIndexQuery` - *Read-only view over the command index document.

Wraps the JSON structure produced by ``scripts.build_command_index`` so

Python primitives (lists/dicts) — never references into the underlying
document — so consumers can safely sort or extend the results.*

- `confidence_from_score` (line 319) `def confidence_from_score(score)` - *Map an unbounded fused recommendation score to a 0-100 display confidence.

:class:`cli.recommendation.RecommendationEngine` produces scores that are
unbounded above because multiple agreeing signals add up, so a raw
percentage would be meaningless. This applies a saturating map
``100 * s / (s + K)`` where ``K`` (:data:`_CONFIDENCE_HALF_SCORE`) is the
score at which confidence reaches 50%. The map is monotonic — more signal
agreement yields higher confidence — and floors at 99 so the display never
claims a dishonest 100%.

#### `recommendation.py`
**Path:** `cli/recommendation.py`

**Classes:**
- `EngineWeights` (line 67) `class EngineWeights` - *Immutable fusion parameters shared by every recommendation run.

Attributes:
    signal_weights: Global multiplier per concrete-action signal. The recon
        plan ranks highest because it is grounded in a real scan of the
        target; the graph walk and the static kill-chain tables are advisory.
    category_prior_floor: Lowest multiplier a concrete action can receive
        from a cold policy category. Never zero, so a single signal can still
        surface an action the policy has not yet learned to favour.
    category_prior_span: Width added on top of the floor for a maximally
        confident policy category. ``floor + span`` is the hottest prior.
    neutral_prior: Multiplier applied to actions whose category carries no
        policy signal at all.
    category_recommendation_weight: Score assigned to a standalone strategic
        category recommendation so it ranks below concrete actions of similar
        confidence while remaining visible.*

produces a high-confidence :class:`Proposal` for the most impactful next
action.

Gap detection rules (ordered by priority):
    - Host in EXPLOITED state without privesc output: recommend
      linpeas/winpeas.
    - Host in OWNED state without credential dump: recommend
      mimikatz/secretsdump/lazydump.
    - Scan XML exists but no enumeration: recommend gobuster/ffuf/enum4linux.
    - Credentials exist but no lateral movement: recommend
      crackmapexec/psexec.*
- `GraphTopologySignal` (line 531) `class GraphTopologySignal` - *Adapt WorldModel network graph pivot_candidates into lateral movement proposals.

Reads the degree-centrality pivot candidates computed by the WorldModel's
NetworkGraph and emits high-confidence proposals for lateral movement,
credential spraying, and network topology exploration — data that was
previously computed but never consumed by the recommendation engine.*

- `ApiKey` (line 75) `class ApiKey` - *Immutable record of a hashed API key bound to a tenant.

The plaintext secret is never stored after creation. Validation
uses constant-time comparison of the SHA-256 hash. ``retired_at``
marks a rotated key: it stays valid for the configured grace
window so live clients keep working during a rotation, then it is
pruned from the store.*
- `ApiKeyStore` (line 161) `class ApiKeyStore` - *Persistent store for tenant-scoped API keys.

Keys are hashed with SHA-256 before storage. Atomic writes use
``.tmp`` + ``os.replace`` to prevent corruption. Rotated keys are
retired (not deleted) so they stay valid during the configured
grace window, then pruned lazily.*

- `require_api_auth` (line 365) `def require_api_auth(store, permissions, require_tenant)` - *Flask-route decorator that enforces API-key + tenant authorization.

The API key is extracted from (in priority order):
1. ``Authorization: Bearer <key>`` header
2. ``X-API-Key`` header
3. ``api_key`` query parameter

If *permissions* is provided the key must hold every listed permission.
If *require_tenant* is ``True`` the key must be scoped to a valid
tenant; when omitted it defaults to
:data:`ApiAuthzConfig.require_tenant_scope` so the security posture
lives in one place.

On failure the decorated route returns a JSON body with ``401`` or
``403`` — never an HTML error page and never ``abort()``, so the
contract holds even in apps with ``TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS`` enabled.*

The proxy is returned by :func:`optional_import` and :func:`optional_attr`

subscription, length) raises :class:`MissingDependencyError` with

    min_value: Optional inclusive lower bound for numeric fields.

Issues are returned as a list so consumers can render them as a table,

    value: The raw value that produced the issue. Sensitive fields are

immediately. ``SO_REUSEADDR`` is set so that a recent close on the
same tuple does not raise a spurious ``EADDRINUSE``. The probe
refuses to bind a wildcard address unless the operator has
explicitly enabled :attr:`SecurityConfig.allow_unspecified_bind`,
so the function doubles as a fail-closed sanitizer for the bind
candidate flowing in from operator-controlled payload values.

Args:
    address: IPv4 address literal to test.
    port: Port number to test. ``0`` lets the kernel pick.
    sock_type: ``socket.SOCK_STREAM`` for TCP services or
        ``socket.SOCK_DGRAM`` for UDP services such as DNS.

Returns:
    Tuple ``(success, errno_value)`` where ``errno_value`` is the
    ``OSError.errno`` on failure and ``None`` on success. Returns
    ``(False, errno.EACCES)`` when the address is a wildcard and
    the operator has not opted in to all-interface binding.*
- `_resolve_bind_address` (line 354) `def _resolve_bind_address(preferred, port, sock_type)` - *Return an address that can actually be bound to on this host.

Probes each candidate with :func:`_probe_bind` and returns the first
address that succeeds. The resolver fails closed: the unspecified
address ``0.0.0.0`` is only ever offered when the operator has set
``allow_unspecified_bind`` in :class:`SecurityConfig`. When every
candidate fails the probe, the configured loopback fallback is
returned so the caller never accidentally binds to every interface.
The probe uses the same socket type the caller will use, so UDP
services such as DNS are tested with ``SOCK_DGRAM``.

Args:
    preferred: Explicit address to try first. When ``None`` the
        address chosen by :func:`_listen_address` is used.
    port: Port number for the probe. When ``0`` the kernel assigns
        an ephemeral port so the test never collides with the real
        service.
    sock_type: Socket type matching the eventual server.

Returns:
    A bindable IPv4 address literal. Guaranteed to be the loopback
    when no other candidate succeeds and the operator has not
    explicitly opted in to binding on every interface.*

The DNS server is optional and runs in a daemon thread, so any
uncaught exception in this function would be surfaced by the
threading runtime onto stderr and pollute the operator's terminal.
All errors are therefore funnelled through the logger and the
function returns cleanly instead of letting the thread crash.

Binding is attempted only after a UDP probe confirms the chosen
address is available, which avoids the common ``EADDRNOTAVAIL``
failure seen when ``lhost`` points to an inactive VPN interface.

- `_resolve_secure_template_path` (line 3777) `def _resolve_secure_template_path(template_name)` - *Return an absolute path strictly contained inside the template folder.

Operator-supplied template names are never trusted. The resolver
enforces three independent gates so a missed upstream check still
fails closed:

1. The shared :func:`validate_template_name` validator rejects
   traversal sequences, length abuse, and disallowed characters.
2. The basename is rebuilt from a local ``re.fullmatch`` group so
   the value joined into the filesystem ``Path`` is a literal
   derived from the regex match rather than the raw input.
3. The rebuilt basename must exist in the precomputed allowlist of
   template files actually present on disk, so any value that
   slipped past the regex still cannot reach :meth:`Path.is_file`.

Args:
    template_name: A template basename. Must match
        :data:`lazyc2.security.constants.TEMPLATE_NAME_PATTERN`.

Returns:

    basename fails validation, escapes ``app.template_folder`` or
    does not exist.*

Subclasses must:

be tested without booting the backend.*

**Classes:**
- `_PayloadSettableProxy` (line 365) `class _PayloadSettableProxy` - *Attribute view over a payload mapping for cmd2 ``Settable`` targets.

cmd2's ``Settable`` reads and writes its bound attribute on a
*target object* (``getattr`` / ``setattr``). LazyOwn keeps its
runtime configuration in a plain ``dict`` (``self.params``) so this
proxy bridges the two: every attribute read or write is delegated to
the underlying dict, which keeps ``set <key> <value>`` and
``assign <key> <value>`` operating on the same backing store with no
drift between them.*
- `LazyOwnShell` (line 395) `class LazyOwnShell(Cmd)` - *A custom interactive shell for the LazyOwn Framework.
This class extends the Cmd class to provide an interactive command-line
interface for the LazyOwn Framework. It supports various commands and
modules related to security and network operations. The shell is initialized
with a set of parameters and scripts, allowing users to execute predefined
functions and manage tasks within the framework.

Attributes:
    prompt (str): The command prompt for the shell, obtained from the
                  `getprompt()` function.
    intro (str): A welcome message and disclaimer displayed when the shell
                 starts, with information about the framework and its usage.
    aliases (dict): A dictionary of command aliases for easier access to
                    frequently used commands.
    params (dict): A dictionary of parameters with their default values,
                   used for configuring various aspects of the framework.
    scripts (list): A list of script names included in the toolkit, representing
                    the available modules and functionalities.
    output (str): An empty string for storing output or results from executed
                  commands or scripts.
    custom_prompt (str): A custom prompt for the shell, obtained from the
                         `getprompt()` function.

Methods:
    __init__(): Initializes the shell with default parameters, script names,
                and an empty output string. Sets up the command prompt and
                custom prompt.*

aliases, and pipelines without modifying ``payload.json`` or

- `DetectionOracle` (line 323) `class DetectionOracle(IDetectionOracle)` - *Maps a (command, args, action_category) triple to a detection probability.

Matching algorithm
------------------
1. Scan all sigma rules for keyword hits in the lowercased command+args.
2. Include rules whose category_tags overlap with action_category.
3. Boost matched rule probabilities by 10% when both keyword AND category hit.
4. Aggregate using the OR-probability formula:
       P = 1 - prod(1 - effective_p_i)
5. Clamp result to [0.0, 1.0].
6. Fall back to _CATEGORY_BASE_PROBABILITY when no rules matched.*
